notes.title: Patch Notes 2.0.2
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45117697/2527fae7da6b1529e12dd29a2e76ba210ed56681.png[/img]

Greetings!

First up, we'd like to start by thanking you all for sharing your thoughts, feedback and kind words with us in the wake of the Total War: PHARAOH DYNASTIES release back in July. It has thoroughly warmed our hearts to see so many of you enjoying the game and hearing your many stories of epic victory (and in some cases crushing defeat, but hey who's counting?).

We just launched Patch 2.0.2, bringing with it a hefty number of fixes, tweaks and balances to further improve your gameplay experience.

[url=https://community.creative-assembly.com/total-war/total-war-pharaoh/blogs/31-total-war-pharaoh-dynasties-patch-notes-2-0-2=button][h3]📜 Read full Patch Notes 2.0.2 here[/h3][/url]

See you on the battlefield!

— The [i]Total War[/i] Team

[hr][/hr][hr][/hr][h1]⚠ IMPORTANT[/h1][hr][/hr][hr][/hr]
If you experience any issues after downloading the update, please take a moment to [b]Verify the integrity of the game files[/b] first to ensure there were no issues when downloading. A step-by-step guide can be found in [url=https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/0C48-FCBD-DA71-93EB]this article[/url].

If the issues persist, please [url=https://support.sega.com/hc/requests/new?ticket_form_id=360003117578]visit our support site[/url] for additional troubleshooting steps and assistance.

Please note that user-generated mods may have compatibility issues with new game updates. If you are encountering performance or stability issues following a release, is recommended that you disable any mods you're running. If you continue to experience issues, please [url=https://support.sega.com/hc/requests/new?ticket_form_id=360003117578]visit our support site[/url] for additional troubleshooting steps and assistance.

notes.title: Hotfix 2.0.1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45117697/c4d33f00cfa713b2502954dae70edd66e5c3e1d6.png[/img]

Greetings folks, 

We hope you’ve all been enjoying the Dynasties update so far! We’ve just rolled out hotfix 2.0.1 to address a few issues that have been identified in the wake of release. 

Here’s what we’ve got for you:

[hr][/hr]
[list]
[*] Fixed a crash that occurred when adding an apostrophe while editing a law text field in Ancient Legacy Hammurabi. 
[*] Fixed issues with Shuffle Commands option for minor factions 
[*] Fixed a crash when trying to change the epithet of the ruler 
[*] Turns per Year and Seasonal Effects are no longer incorrectly overridden when loading a game 
[*] (Continuing old campaigns will allow for the correct progression of years, but some already present issues in existing saves may remain.) 
[*] Adjustments to end-turn sequence performance to avoid extreme frame-rate drops 
[*] Fixed a UI bug where 'The Dynasty Tree' and 'Dynasties' tabs could disappear, making the feature inaccessible.
[i]This is caused when an heir from another faction, who is not a blood relative to the dynasty ruler, succeeds the Supreme Ruler. In such case the heir character appears to not to be part of a Dynasty anymore. This could potentially result in further issues with the Dynasty system in the Campaign. [b]The fix will apply to new campaigns only, or if the player reloads a save game from before the issue occurred.[/b][/i]
[*] Aegean and Mesopotamian factions can now trade battle legitimacy 
[*] Fixed an issue for horde factions where the new faction leader would not be spawned on the map when the old leader dies 
[*] Fixed an issue where the passive command of Iolaos that provides War Spoils rank buff was not working 
[*] Fixed an issue where the ‘Plans Within Plans - Playing as Bay, complete 10 Intrigues in the Hittite Court’ achievement was not working 
[*] Fixed an issue where the ‘Counter Plots’ deed was not working 
[*] Added missing logo to Photo Mode 
[/list]
[hr][/hr]
We also wanted to acknowledge that many of you have raised some concerns around balance – thank you for your feedback. We’re going to quickly address the core topics for you here: 

[h3]Anti Player Bias Reports[/h3]

We’re actively investigating reports and would very much appreciate your help in identifying bugs that are causing adverse behaviours. Please report them here: https://community.creative-assembly.com/total-war/total-war-pharaoh/forums/1-general-discussion/threads/6493-dynasties-campaign-ai-feedback-needed 

[h3]Issues with AI Army Production[/h3] 

While we don’t think there are any bugs with the systems at play here, we do realise that some fine tuning is required on easier difficulties. Rest assured that realise many players do enjoy the difficulty of the game and so we intend to ensure any balance changes are appropriate for the difficulty settings players have picked. 

In the meantime, we wanted to take the opportunity to direct players to these settings when creating campaigns, which may help tweak the experience to their needs: 

[b]Issues with early game economy:[/b] 

Increase your own starting budget with the setting [b][Campaign][/b] > [b][Player Starting Budget][/b] 

Tweak the AI’s starting budget with the setting [b][AI][/b] > [b][AI Starting Budget] [/b]

Change army upkeep with the setting [b][Campaign][/b] > [b][Player Army Upkeep] [/b]

[b]Issues with the AI producing armies too quickly: [/b]

Increase your own recruitment capacity in the setting [b][Campaign][/b] > [b][Player Recruitment Capacity][/b] 

Decrease the AI recruitment capacity in the setting [b][AI][/b] > [b][Recruitment Capacity][/b] 

[h3]Issues with Lethality[/h3]

We’re also aware that while many of you are enjoying the lethality system, some of you are feeling like it’s not hitting quite right. Again, we are investigating the most ideal way to ensure all players can play the game with a system that feels right for them, whether that’s incredibly lethal battles, or some a bit more forgiving. In the meantime, there is a setting players can experiment with to adjust lethality in battles.

Try disabling it to see if you prefer it off with the setting [b][Battle][/b] > [b][Lethality Chance][/b] 

[hr][/hr]

Thanks to everyone who reported bugs and given feedback since launch! If you run into any issues after updating to 2.0.1 please be sure to report them over in our [url=https://community.totalwar.com/pharaoh-support]dedicated bug reporting sub-forum[/url]. 

Until next time, we’ll see you on the battlefield! 

—The [i]Total War[/i] Team


[hr][/hr][hr][/hr][h1]⚠ IMPORTANT[/h1][hr][/hr][hr][/hr]
If you experience any issues after downloading the update, please take a moment to [b]Verify the integrity of the game files[/b] first to ensure there were no issues when downloading. A step-by-step guide can be found in [url=https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/0C48-FCBD-DA71-93EB]this article[/url].

If the issues persist, please [url=https://support.sega.com/hc/requests/new?ticket_form_id=360003117578]visit our support site[/url] for additional troubleshooting steps and assistance.

[hr][/hr][hr][/hr][h1]🧱 MOD WARNING[/h1][hr][/hr][hr][/hr]
Please note that user-generated mods may have compatibility issues with new game updates. If you are encountering performance or stability issues following a release, is recommended that you disable any mods you're running. If you continue to experience issues, please [url=https://support.sega.com/hc/requests/new?ticket_form_id=360003117578]visit our support site[/url] for additional troubleshooting steps and assistance.

notes.title: Total War: PHARAOH Update - Announce
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45117697/2d0cfe9cc5af9e128384740c5c9ab5cd065f993d.png[/img]

Hello, Total War Community!

We hope the valiant Montu has brought victories to those of you who braved the battlefields of Ancient Egypt, Anatolia and the Levant, while the wisdom of Toth will bolster the decisiveness of those who are yet to thread those ancient fields of destruction.

In January we launched the High Tide Update for Total War: PHARAOH, welcoming the harbingers of the Bronze-Age Collapse, the Sea Peoples, as a new playable culture alongside their two dedicated factions, bringing the core roster up to ten. We were delighted to see your positive reception to this free update which was part of our post-launch ambitions to create a vast Bronze-Age strategy experience.

As mentioned in our Leadership Message back in December, the vision for Total War: PHARAOH since the outset of the project has been to increase the size of the campaign map and introduce even more cultures and ways of engaging in glorious strategic conquest. Today, we’re excited to announce that this will come courtesy of a vast free update that significantly reworks the existing campaign mode already available in PHARAOH’s base-game. This update will usher in a host of exciting new additions whilst also implementing some familiar content from its Bronze-Age brother, A Total War Saga: TROY. We want to improve your experience of this most iconic age, and we’re working hard to deliver it later this year.

In terms of the content you can expect to experience, prepare to embark on a conquest across a map that has greatly increased in size as we add the renowned and highly requested regions of Mesopotamia and the Aegean to the conflict alongside the playable cultures of Babylon, Assyria, Mycenae and Troy. Whilst within the strategic campaign layer, you will have access to all new mechanics such as the Dynasty system which adds mortality and succession to the faction leaders’ quest to leave behind a legacy that will survive the ages. And finally, within battle you can expect over 80 new units for the Mesopotamian factions, alongside the addition of over 70 reworked units from a Total War Saga: TROY.

Given that this update will make some big changes to the way in which Total War: PHARAOH plays, we will be taking steps to ensure that you still have the choice to experience the original campaign should you wish to. We’ll reveal more information on how this will be achieved in a later instalment.

On another note, we’ve made it clear that we’re keen to improve the level of transparency we exhibit across all our products to ensure that you have a better understanding of what we’re working on, as well as how and why we make certain design decisions. With this in mind, we want you to come on this Bronze-Age journey with us to help us begin to find the right path to a greater developer-community collaboration.

Starting next week, we'll be kicking off a series of conversations around the creation of this update, starting with a deep dive looking into the expanded campaign map and how we're aiming to bring this long-lost world to life, before inviting you all to send us your questions for a Q&A session the following week.

Every couple of weeks, we'll have a new topic featuring a variety of voices from across the project, first detailing how we're approaching the work, and inviting you to share your thoughts and feedback on that vision. We'll then come back to you the week after to dive into more detail on the topic over on the official Total War Discord - so make sure you join today and keep an eye out for new channels to post your hotly anticipated questions.

Thanks again for your support, and for your candid feedback - we want Total War: PHARAOH to be an incredible experience for everyone!

—The [i]Total War[/i] Team
